title: Massepe (Thurston's Creek)
summary: Massepe is a Jamaica, Queens placename for a river or creek, probably the waterway later known as Thurston's Creek or Thurston Basin.
map_geometry_source: Approximate modern Thurston Basin point from TopoZone/USGS topographic listing; not an exact historical Massepe coordinate.
introduction_content: Massepe is associated with a river or creek in the southern part of the former Town of Jamaica.
translation_content:
Massepe is interpreted as a great or long river, from elements meaning great or large and river. Related language comparisons include forms for river in several Algonquian languages, including Unkechaug and Mohegan.

Why Place Names Matter

“People name places for various reasons, such as describing, honoring figures, commemorating historical events, narrating incidents, and adapting names through time.”

— Yoko Kugo, Community Voices, Practices, and Memories in Environmental Communication (2022), Chapter introduction
whereintheworld_content: Map location note: The pin uses modern Thurston Basin coordinates for the probable Thurston's Creek association and is not an exact historical coordinate for the 1657 Massepe waterway.
